newsitem.title: THAILAND: Loxley delays new investments on economy.
newsitem.headline: Loxley delays new investments on economy.

text.p: Loxley Plc said on Thursday it will delay new investments in 1997 and adopt a cautious business strategy due to the sagging economy.
"We will delay any new domestic and overseas investments this year. We all know the economy is unfavourable to invest," Loxley president Dhongchai Lamsam told a news conference.
"However Loxley will carry on with its existing projects such as paging services in the Philippines and Sri Lanka.
Loxley is a large diversified public company with interests in telecommunications, computer, trading and construction materials.
Loxley would also implement and adopt a cautious strategy this year to prevent a rise in bad debts, he said.

"We will not care how much our sales and profits will rise this year. Under the current conditions, what we are concerned about is the ability to collect all of the payments from our customers," Dhongchai said.
He said Loxley's telecommunication project in North Korea was under way and had good potential.
"Our project in North Korea is good. We have installed 2,000 telephones lines and are beginning to sell those lines," he said.
Loxley won a 30-year concession from the North Korean government in late 1995 to install a telecommunication network in Rajin Sonbong Free Economic and Trade Zone.
Dhongchai did not say how much the project was worth.
Loxley also has a joint investment with Broken Hill Pty (BHP) Co Ltd of Australia to build a cold-rolled steel plant in Rayong province, east of Bangkok.
BHP holds 75 percent stake in the project, while Loxley owns the rest.
The plant which is scheduled to complete late this year will have nominal capacity of 300,000 tonnes of steel per year.
"The oversupply of steel in the world market will not affect our plant. All of the plant's production is already ordered," Dhongchai said.
